alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction lowers DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. Patient started carbamazepine 2 weeks ago while on DTG-based TLD. Viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence, consistent with subtherapeutic DTG. The temporal relationship (virological rebound only after carbamazepine addition) strongly supports drug interaction as the cause. The clinician's plan does not address this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch carbamazepine to valproic acid per guidelines, or consult neurology for alternative antiepileptic. Repeat viral load after adjustment.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatraemia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), hyponatraemia (Na 128 mmol/L), ataxia, nystagmus, and tremor. These findings are consistent with carbamazepine toxicity. Sodium valproate is also prescribed; valproate can potentiate carbamazepine toxicity via pharmacokinetic interactions. The clinician plans dose reduction and repeat level, which is appropriate. Hyponatraemia may also relate to carbamazepine-induced SIADH.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat level, and monitor sodium. Consider switching to valproic acid monotherapy per guideline interaction advice.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires adherence assessment
alerts.message: Guidelines state virological monitoring provides early indication of treatment failure and the need to switch regimens. Patient's viral load became detectable at 1,240 copies/mL after prior suppression. While the carbamazepine-DTG interaction is a likely contributor, guidelines require thorough adherence assessment and repeat viral load to distinguish drug interaction from treatment failure. The clinician's plan does not include a repeat viral load or enhanced adherence counselling.

evidence.recommended_action: Conduct enhanced adherence assessment and repeat viral load in 2–3 months after resolving the drug interaction. Evaluate for resistance if persistently detectable.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT with hepatotoxic polypharmacy
alerts.message: Patient has ALT 68 U/L (elevated). Both carbamazepine and sodium valproate are known hepatotoxic agents. TDF can also cause hepatic toxicity per guidelines, which recommend LFTs and RFTs when deranged. The recent carbamazepine addition 2 weeks ago provides temporal support for drug-induced liver injury. However, valproate has been used longer without documented baseline ALT, making pre-existing elevation possible. Monitoring trend is needed.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat ALT and LFTs within 1–2 weeks. If ALT rises further, consider holding carbamazepine or valproate and consult hepatology.
